Ben / Marissa — looping you in. Vendor reports they clicked a forwarded invite from their shared orders mailbox and are hitting a session lock once SSO returns. Redstone procurement is waiting on W-9 acceptance.

What I observed / hypothesize: forwarded messages can change "From" or display name metadata; if the invite token or the portal relies on a tight NameID match during SAML handshake we could see a mismatch. If the portal binds the invite token to an expected subject NameID (email) but the IdP returns the distribution address or a different displayName then the portal may treat it as a different principal and block.

Please confirm whether we currently: 
- bind invite tokens to the original recipient email at time-of-send, AND
- strictly require returned SAML NameID to match that address.

Next steps: can we provide a quick workaround (reissue invite to the direct user email or allow vendor to accept via a 'claim account' flow) and a fix for tokens that survive forwarding?

Jonas

Thanks for the details. Quick summary of what I pulled from the trace and saml debug: attached saml-debug.log.

Findings:
- The invite token (server-side) is bound to the originally invited email (procure@lynxsupplies.com) and a short-lived nonce.
- When the vendor forwarded the email from orders@lynxsupplies.com the mail client caused the browser to hit the link with a different referrer and, crucially, the IdP returned a NameID of orders@lynxsupplies.com rather than procure@lynxsupplies.com.
- Our post-SSO handler verifies the NameID against the invite recipient; mismatch triggers an account protection branch that shows the session-lock page and prevents token consumption. That path currently requires manual operator override or a fresh invite.

Workarounds we can do right now:
1) Resend the invite directly to the user's personal mailbox (sara.torres@lynxsupplies.com) — will avoid distribution alias.
2) Issue a short-lived 'accept via code' link we can validate against a phone OTP.

I attached saml-debug.log and added a short repro note to the trace folder (Drive link above). For the longer fix we should:
- Make invite acceptance tolerant of canonicalized emails (strip DisplayName and subaddressing) OR
- Add a guided flow if NameID != invite-recipient to allow a one-click confirmation by the vendor that they control both addresses.

I can reissue invite from the portal now if you want me to.
